Synopsis: The players approach the drow commander at the goblin camp, escorted by a goblin who they rescued from a nearby druid grove. The drow is seeking that grove and upon learning its location from the goblin will prepare to raid it, demanding that the player help. If the goblin recognises that the player is a True Soul - a figure of authority - her life will be spared. If she does not recognise this, the drow will execute her unless the player intervenes on her behalf. Minthara wields authority and can probe minds; she learns the grove’s location from the goblin and intends to raid it, demanding the player’s cooperation — either by opening the gate and signalling the assault or by refusing and fighting her. context: You and your party have been brought before Nightwarden Minthara in a goblin camp, escorted by Sazza, a goblin you recovered from a nearby druid grove. Minthara is a True Soul with the power to probe minds and quickly appraises both you and the prisoner, concluding the grove (and the tiefling‑occupied intruders) can be found past the bridge to the east by a gate draped in ivy. The captive has already revealed that location, and Minthara demands you help by returning to the grove, opening the gate and signalling her raiding party — or refuse and fight her now. Sazza’s life depends on whether she (or Minthara) recognizes you as a True Soul: recognition will spare her, otherwise Minthara will execute her unless you intervene. Off‑screen fights, druid/bear activity and tensions with goblin leadership explain the urgency and brutality behind Minthara’s orders.
